record.original_question: Let p be a prime number. A group Γ is called p-Jordan if there exist constants J and e such that any finite subgroup G ⊂ Γ contains a normal abelian subgroup of order coprime to p and of index at most J · |G(p) |e. (For example by the results of Brauer–Feit and Larsen–Pink, for any field K of characteristic p the group GLn(K) is p-Jordan with e = 3.) Let the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) of the group Γ be the infimum of all constants e for which the above bound holds for some constant J = J(e). a) Is it true that this infimum is always attained? b) Is it true that e(Γ) ⩽ 3 for any p-Jordan group Γ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a prime number $p$. For a finite group $G$, let $|G_{(p)}|$ denote the order of a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ (equivalently, the largest power of $p$ dividing $|G|$). A group $\Gamma$ is called $p$-Jordan if there exist constants $J \geq 1$ and $e \geq 0$ such that every finite subgroup $G \subseteq \Gamma$ contains a normal abelian subgroup $A 	rianglelefteq G$ whose order is coprime to $p$ and whose index satisfies
$$[G:A] \;\leq\; J\cdot |G_{(p)}|^{e}.$$
(Classical results of Brauer–Feit and Larsen–Pink imply, for instance, that for any field $K$ of characteristic $p$ the group $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ is $p$-Jordan with $e=3$.) Define the $p$-Jordan exponent of a $p$-Jordan group $\Gamma$ by
$$e(\Gamma) \;=\; \inf\{\, e \geq 0 : 	ext{there exists } J=J(e) 	ext{ such that the above bound holds}\,\}.$$

(a) Is the infimum defining $e(\Gamma)$ always attained, i.e. is there always a constant $J$ for which the bound holds with exponent $e(\Gamma)$ itself?

(b) Is it true that $e(\Gamma) \leq 3$ for every $p$-Jordan group $\Gamma$?
